pass_condition: The snapshot's canonical dump hash depends only on that snapshot's repositories rows (R-C: same value INT-W0-4's repositories_dump_hash computes).

findings.statement: The dump hash drops a hardcoded table list instead of keeping only repositories, so on a migrated v1 database the 1,000 legacy_repositories rows are hashed into every v2 snapshot's identity.
findings.failure_scenario: Migrate the real v1 DB, create snapshot 'snapX' with zero repositories rows, then edit one legacy v1 row's owner: the hash moves from ded974e2... to e294351f... -- a v1-only edit changes a v2 snapshot's stored identity, and the same snapshot promoted on a fresh DB and on a migrated DB can never agree.

observations: R-C otherwise holds: both helpers call the identical porchlamp.snapshot.reproduce.canonical_dump_hash on a scratch copy; INT-W0-4's version (porchlamp/lakehouse.py:187) enumerates tables from sqlite_master and drops the excluded set, and its excluded set is frozenset({'snapshot_meta'}).
The follow-up swap to porchlamp.lakehouse.repositories_dump_hash is mechanical only if the v2 helper keeps its extra WHERE snapshot_id=? filter; the two differ in that filter, nothing else.
Fix: keep repositories (an allow-list) instead of dropping a fixed exclude-list.
